I assume it's a fairly low (<1%) number. Is that roughly right? o good question, on my phone rn but <@144468805697929216> also runs a eth2 db - help? 🙂 https://beaconscan.com/stat/slot skipped blocks I guess? Oh, yes, that's great <@!132497957135187968>! Eyeballing it, it actually looks like ~1%! admittingly the incentives to run an eth1 node are not given rn you are more profitable not running an eth1 node on eth2 by like 3% but don’t spread the word on that 😅 Does that assume you use Infura's free tier, or you actually pay for it? doesn’t matter i believe, it influences your attestation voting behavior. <@755590043632140352> did some analysis on that Non-canonical blocks are currently around 1% of total. So if ETH forks does the EF and everything in this channel go with one fork or could they conceivably support and exist for both forks? (This is a what-if question). Depends on the forks I suppose, and it's more of a governance question than a technical question. Even in off-topic, I don't think this server is the right place to speculate without technical context. I did some analysis on slot 0 in the early days of Pyrmont. The one that has even raised an issue about this on the specs is <@!573787335796326400> https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/issues/2152. Answering <@!552133098075193354> no eth1 endpoint at all is more profitable than having one for a small staker at least. Of course using Infura is more profitable than both. But the fact that not having any eth1 endpoint at all is a wining strategy says something about the network right now.
